newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sing Tao reveals losses by newspaper unit.
newsitem.headline: Sing Tao reveals losses by newspaper unit.

text.p: Sing Tao Holdings Ltd said in a statement on Thursday that its unit Hongkong Standard Newspapers Ltd posted operating losses for the year ended March 31, 1996.
"Hongkong Standard...showed an operating loss in excess of the operating loss of approximately HK$11.7 million incurred by the group in newspaper publishing in that year," it said.

Turnover of Hongkong Standard Newspapers Ltd amounted to about HK$190 million, representing about 18 percent of the turnover of Sing Tao and its subsidiaries from newspaper publishing in that year, it added.

Hongkong Standard Newspapers publishes the English-language Hongkong Standard and Hongkong Sunday Standard. It is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Sing Tao Holdings Ltd, which also publishes Chinese-language newspapers.

The statement, carried in the Hongkong Standard newspaper, comes after Hong Kong's Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) on Wednesday raided offices of the daily, alleging it fraudulently inflated its circulation figures.
The ICAC arrested six persons -- four current employees of the Hongkong Standard Newspapers Ltd and two former employees.

The ICAC said on Wednesday it uncovered a scheme involving deliberate excess print runs of more than 10,000 copies per day of the newspaper which were sold to a bogus bulk distributor. The surplus was actually sold as waste paper.
"ICAC inquiries also indicated that more recently the deliberately printed surplus and systematic disposal has ranged from 14,000 up to 23,000 copies per day," the ICAC had said.
